current.text: Yahoo lists him as questionable with a back injury.
Jaxson Hayes started at center in the preseason because Utah does not want Jaren Jackson Jr. playing much center. Filipowski is back in the rotation.
Utah is trying to win this season and has a crowded frontcourt with Jaren Jackson Jr., Lauri Markkanen, Jusuf Nurkic, Jaxson Hayes and Ace Bailey.
His late-season jump last season (162nd before the trade deadline, 39th after) came while Utah was tanking.
Experts do not expect him to start at center. They see no path to the starting job.
His role should shrink on a deeper team that is trying to win. He will not get the 28 minutes he got late last season, and the coach's leash should be shorter.
Sell. One expert says his late-season numbers feel fake and he is only worth a flier around pick 140.

durable.text: He is one of the worst defensive bigs in the NBA and does not rebound well on defense. That makes him a bad fit next to Jaren Jackson Jr.
He has good offensive skills, but experts doubt he is a long-term starting center.
His threes are poor, he has never been a shot blocker, and he gets some steals.
One expert calls his free throw shooting great for a big man, but his projections are only about 73% at the line.

note: Both sites value him at 0 USD (Yahoo rank 204, ESPN rank 145), and nobody drafted him in our league last season. That matches the expert view that his 11.4 points and 7.2 rebounds in 23.4 minutes were inflated by Utah's tanking. He has no strong category and no punt-build fit, so he is at most one of our last picks. More likely he is someone to watch on waivers. Early on, check his back injury and his minutes behind Hayes and Nurkic. He only becomes interesting if a Utah big gets hurt.
